### Contributing guidelines

- [x] I have read [CONTRIBUTING.md](https://github.com/nvim-mini/mini.nvim/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md)
- [x] I have read [CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md](https://github.com/nvim-mini/mini.nvim/blob/main/CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md)
- [x] I have updated 'mini.nvim' to latest version of the `main` branch

### Module(s)

mini.completion

### Neovim version

0.11.x

### Description

When scrolling through the suggestions for complete options, anytime there's a suggestion of type `Text`, the following error happens:

```
Error executing vim.schedule lua callback: ...m/site/pack/deps/start/mini.nvim/lua/mini/completion.lua:1917: attempt to index local 'lsp_item' (a nil value)
stack traceback:
        ...m/site/pack/deps/start/mini.nvim/lua/mini/completion.lua:1917: in function 'normalize_item_doc'
        ...m/site/pack/deps/start/mini.nvim/lua/mini/completion.lua:1450: in function 'info_window_lines'
        ...m/site/pack/deps/start/mini.nvim/lua/mini/completion.lua:1401: in function ''
        vim/_editor.lua: in function <vim/_editor.lua:0>
```

It's important to note that in my testing, it **only** happens with `ts_ls` language server. However, other completion plugins don't seem to have this problem.

### Reproduction

1. Create separate 'nvim-repro' config directory:
    - '~/.config/nvim-repro/' on Unix
    - '~/AppData/Local/nvim-repro/' on Windows

2. Inside 'nvim-repro' directory create a file named 'init.lua'.
   Populate it with the following content:

```lua
-- Clone latest 'mini.nvim' (requires Git CLI installed)
vim.cmd('echo "Installing `mini.nvim`" | redraw')
local mini_path = vim.fn.stdpath('data') .. '/site/pack/deps/start/mini.nvim'
local clone_cmd = { 'git', 'clone', '--depth=1', 'https://github.com/nvim-mini/mini.nvim', mini_path }
vim.fn.system(clone_cmd)
vim.cmd('echo "`mini.nvim` is installed" | redraw')

-- Make sure 'mini.nvim' is available
vim.cmd('packadd mini.nvim')
require('mini.deps').setup()
require('mini.completion').setup() -- use default config

-- Add extra setup steps needed to reproduce the behavior
-- Use `MiniDeps.add('user/repo')` to install another plugin from GitHub
MiniDeps.add("neovim/nvim-lspconfig")
MiniDeps.add("pmizio/typescript-tools.nvim")
MiniDeps.add("nvim-lua/plenary.nvim")

require("typescript-tools").setup {}
vim.lsp.enable("ts_ls")
```

3. Run `NVIM_APPNAME=nvim-repro nvim` (i.e. execute `nvim` with `NVIM_APPNAME` environment variable set to "nvim-repro").
   Wait for all dependencies to install.

4. Replace this with description of interactive reproduction steps along with the behavior you observe.
    Open a javascript file and get a suggestion of type `Text` to complete.

Thanks for the issue!

> 4\. Open a javascript file and get a suggestion of type `Text` to complete.

Can you please provide (copy directly if small, link otherwise) an exact example of where I can get `Text` type of candidates with the provided setup? I tried in several simple test files and couldn't get any `Text` candidates.

Here's a example:

```js
const greet = "Hello world"

// try doing greet. And there should a suggestion called greet of type text
greet.
```

It's important note that those are not real methods, I notice this previously too. Don't know why `greet` is shown as a complete suggestion. But the problem is that when scrolling through through suggestion, this error shows up really often.    

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/0c64f360-ae41-4c57-b122-bf92765ce02f

> Here's a example:
> 
> const greet = "Hello world"
> 
> // try doing greet. And there should a suggestion called greet of type text
> greet.

Unfortunately, still can not reproduce getting the `Text` candidate. Here is a screencast:

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/3ad5c9b4-c783-4235-b8c5-04c53950f404

My current guess is that 'pmizio/typescript-tools.nvim' somehow modifies candidates, but I'd need a way to reproduce the issue to investigate further.

Maybe there is a user-wide or project-wide configuration of the LSP server that affects this?

Okay thanks for your time. I really can't figure out what's going on. There's no user or project wide config. I guess I'll close for now. It has to be something on my system because I can reproduce with that minimal example.

> Okay thanks for your time. I really can't figure out what's going on. There's no user or project wide config. I guess I'll close for now. It has to be something on my system because I can reproduce with that minimal example.

I mean, the error still shouldn't happen if everything plays well with each other.

If you have aspiration, we can try to debug on your side. The first thing I'd do is add logging and check the actual value which causes the error. The following diff should do the trick:

```diff
diff --git a/lua/mini/completion.lua b/lua/mini/completion.lua
index 9afe4858..c52d840e 100644
--- a/lua/mini/completion.lua
+++ b/lua/mini/completion.lua
@@ -1433,6 +1433,8 @@ H.show_info_window = vim.schedule_wrap(function(info_id)
   end)
 end)
 
+_G.log = {}
+
 H.info_window_lines = function(info_id)
   local completed_item = H.info.event.completed_item
   local info = completed_item.info or ''
@@ -1447,6 +1449,7 @@ H.info_window_lines = function(info_id)
 
   -- Try to get documentation from LSP's latest resolved info
   if H.info.lsp.status == 'received' then
+    table.insert(_G.log, vim.deepcopy({ info_lsp = H.info.lsp, completed_item = completed_item }))
     local lines = H.normalize_item_doc(H.info.lsp.result, info)
     H.info.lsp.status = 'done'
     return lines
```

These changes need to be applied to the 'lua/mini/completion.lua' file inside the directory that you have 'mini.nvim' / 'mini.completion' installed. After that:
- Restart.
- Reproduce the error.
- Execute `:=_G.log` and paste here the last list item (should be a table with `info_lsp` and `completed_item` fields).

@maddie-m, can you please make sure that you are on latest `main` and provide the full error message?
If possible, could you also provide (as concise as possible) steps of how to reproduce? In particular:
- Name and version of LSP server.
- How it and 'mini.completion are set up.
- Which project/file to open, where to put cursor, and which keys to press.

---

Note to self. Making sure that this error is not triggered is probably not complicated: using `H.normalize_item_doc(H.info.lsp.result or {}, info)` [here](https://github.com/nvim-mini/mini.nvim/blob/fbb6ad02871d296fc7d3ebd453e1be89b1210f68/lua/mini/completion.lua#L1483) should work here. But trying to search for  the actual culprit is more valuable (and leads to a more useful test).

@rafamadriz, @maddie-m, I *think* this should be resolved on latest `main` after resolving #2090. See [this comment](https://github.com/nvim-mini/mini.nvim/issues/2090#issuecomment-3457571647) for the possible root cause.
